chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
It does not behove a servant to have trust in two conditions: health and wealth; you see him healthy, then he falls ill, and you see him rich, then he becomes poor.
ai.seo_question: What two things should a person not trust in according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against placing ultimate trust in the transient states of health and wealth, noting that their sudden reversal serves as a reminder of human vulnerability. This teaching aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-'afiyah* not as a permanent possession but as a temporary test, urging believers to anchor their reliance in the Eternal rather than the ephemeral. The warning underscores the impermanence of worldly conditions, encouraging spiritual preparedness for inevitable change.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 426. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon them, said:

It does not behove a man to have trust in two positions, health and riches, because there is many a man whom you see healthy but he soon falls sick and many a man whom you see rich but soon turns destitute.
